missing_caveats: Every verifier number is a single run at a single seed (search, engine, sched, robustness, compute-allocation, contention, agentic-value); 04-conflicts.md (f): 'Both repos are single-seed for every headline number' with ~1.7x Modal box-to-box wall-clock variance noted for dexa runs.

Compute-allocation N=1 baseline (0.689) was decoded greedily (temperature 0.0) while N=4/16 used 0.8 (modal_eval_compute.py:114); the '0.69 -> 0.90' lever mixes decoding regimes, and pass@k is an oracle selector (sampling ceiling), labeled 'directional, not a leaderboard'.

The weak-verifier robustness result (93-96%, 3.04-3.52x) is post-hoc token accounting (es_b4 over one n=16 generation), not the live scheduler; ledger caveat also records 6-10 problems per model with no visible pass within N=16 in addition to the 7.7%/3.8% visible false-positive rates.
The continuous scheduler (2.63x/2.12x) was run only on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct; Qwen2.5-Coder-7B (the MVP model) has no in-engine measurement.

Verification in modal_verifier_sched.py is synchronous inside engine.step() (a python subprocess per sample, up to 10 s timeout), so the 86.6 s wall already includes serialized verify time; per-verify latency is not logged anywhere, and the engine script's 27.0 s / 18.6 s verify walls use any()-short-circuited verification.

The round engine's own docstring labels its wall-clock 'directional (prefix-cache state persists across calls)' and names decode tokens as the primary metric; the 1.53x figure carries that label in the repo.

Both engine and sched runs put the naive baseline second on a warm prefix cache; the RESULTS.md sections do not state this (only the script docstrings do), so a reader of RESULTS.md alone cannot see the bias.

max_model_len 4096, enforce_eager (no CUDA graphs) and gpu_memory_utilization 0.9 for the sched run; nothing at long shared prefixes was measured with the scheduler; eager mode is noted by the ledger to compress the vLLM n>1 pathology ratio (understates).

SGLang and LMCache versions are unpinned in every SGLang/LMCache eval (ledger provenance paragraph); the SGLang gate's 4k n=1 point landed in timing noise and its first measurement was polluted by RadixAttention caching before fix 4c4bc9f.

Contention v2 used W=4k only, k=2 derived from an assumed pass probability p (k = ceil(1/p)), distinct per-agent contexts (no cross-agent prefix sharing), and a simulated verifier; agentic-value v1 notes early-stop 'runs branches in sequential waves, so it can increase latency on harder turns'.

Ledger status labels differ from the brief's grouping: agentic-serving-value-v1 and sglang-gate are FALSIFIED theses (numbers reused as bounds), contention-v2 is BOUNDED; the brief's 'Bounded / contradicted' heading does not carry the FALSIFIED labels.

Section 12 (session-stateful combination) relies on stateful-session numbers whose in-engine runs are capped at 16k; the 32k-64k restore-vs-prefill figures are HF tensor-copy measurements (Qwen2.5-7B, single request), and docs/RESULTS.md records the Dexa connector losing to vLLM re-prefill at 8k and under 16-24-way concurrency (04-conflicts.md conflicts 1-4).

voice-inference harness reuse: all GPU data is seed 1 on an L40S with synthetic traces (every distribution marked 'assumption'); prompts are synthetic token ids with no tokenizer or output-quality measurement; pcie/hbm/resident_wait counters are sim-only and read zero in GPU runs; manifests record git_sha 'unknown' and no connector/config provenance; pytest-asyncio is an unlisted dependency (12/27 tests fail without it).

dexa_platform reuse: 29 unit tests only, no integration test against a live backend; no payment/Stripe path, signup trusts provider/subject JSON (no OAuth), management endpoints authenticate with the inference API key, no rate limiting/retries/idempotency, Dockerfile omits control/ and sessions/; metering is per token and per-request cost telemetry is image-token pricing for a VLM gateway.

Morph facts are largely self-reported: 10,500 tok/s and 98% accuracy are Morph's own B200 numbers (OpenRouter observed 1,537 tps P50); WarpGrep SWE-Bench Pro lifts are Morph's evaluations with methodology pages blocked (HTTP 429); 'forked from vLLM' is stated only for Reflexes; standby tier is GLM-5.3 only; revenue/team figures are tweets and job posts.

Fireworks 350 ms TTFT is an Inworld-reported case study (medium confidence), not a Fireworks-published figure; Cursor/Kimi/Fireworks partnership is Moonshot's statement, not confirmed by Cursor; Kimi K2.7 Code / GLM-5.2 serving support is a medium-confidence secondary source.
Tensormesh: FAQ says the SaaS is 'in beta' while the May 2026 press release says 'general availability'; $2.50/hr H200 is reserved capacity 'via Nebius and Yotta'; no customers named.

Wafer Pass prices are from the April 2026 launch with per-5-hour request caps; whether they are unchanged as of Sept 2026 is listed as unknown; MI355X $2.29-$2.95 is a rental range Wafer cites, not a cloud list price.

OpenHands' recommendation also lists LM Studio and Ollama, minimum context 22,000, and a 24 GB quantized GPU or 64 GB Apple Silicon target; TraceLab's sample is 43 developers; the Codex $15.9 case is Azure OpenAI with in_memory retention.
overall: The brief's repo-side numbers are accurate: every headline figure (0.884=0.884, 2.63x, 2.12x, round-engine 2.60x/1.53x/0.878 vs 0.896/18.6 vs 27.0 s, post-hoc 0.909/860,830, robustness 0.909/0.848/93%/7.7%/2.85x/3.04x and 0.963/0.921/96%/3.8%/3.45x/3.52x, compute-allocation 0.689/0.829/0.902 and 52k->858k, TriviaQA 0.680->0.693, contention 1.38/1.69/1.87x, agentic-value 1.4/5.0/11.5x and 1.00/1.01/1.02x, vLLM 174x vs SGLang 2.2x/1.04x, line numbers 43/79/127, 194 lines, 29 and 27 tests) reproduces from evals/RESULTS.md, the scripts, the ledgers and the build inventory, and the proven/bounded/superseded labels follow the ledger. The competitive-table and research figures (Morph, Relace, Cognition, Fireworks, Wafer, Tensormesh, TraceLab, Mooncake, OpenHands, Anthropic/OpenAI TTLs, Managed Agents, MI355X) all trace to the 05-research files. Defects found: (1) 'seed 0' is wrong for the sched run (per-sample seeds 1..16) and 'fixed seeds across scripts' is wrong (seeds and request shapes differ per script); (2) baseline (d) mislabels SGLang RadixAttention caching as 'LMCache'; (3) 'all engine measurements ... vLLM 0.24.0' omits that the load/long-prefix numbers are on unpinned SGLang; (4) the '10 ms HumanEval verify' figure is a bad derivation (any() short-circuits, so 27.0 s / 2,624 is not per-verify latency) and the 5-60 s repo range is unsourced; (5) the section-9 table attaches SWE-grep-mini's 2,800 tok/s to SWE-grep (650); (6) a Wafer paraphrase is presented in quotation marks; (7) section 12 calls prefix caching and early-stop 'additive' when the repo measured 1.00-1.02x GPU-seconds for early-stop on an idle GPU; (8) the MVP model Qwen2.5-Coder-7B has only a post-hoc measurement, never the in-engine scheduler. The unproven-table costs are unsupported but labeled as estimates, which the rules permit. Most significant omitted caveats: single-seed/single-run for every number, the greedy N=1 baseline, post-hoc (not live) weak-verifier costs, synchronous in-loop verification, the FALSIFIED ledger labels on agentic-value v1 and the SGLang gate, and the self-reported nature of Morph's throughput and benchmark figures.
